items.title: 52240_Frank _Machito_ Grillo oral history interview
items.q: we were supposed to play for Charlie Parker, but Charlie Parker got sick and was replaced by Sonny Stitt.

ctx.x: Well, the peole start to rave about the commotion of our rhythm section create because they knew about jazz, but they never had that in a battle. The jazz was played by a bass and a drummer and the usual jazz; but, and then when you put a conga and bongo and timbales and maracas and senserro or cow bells, you know, there are so many syn-copation involved that the people they just went crazy.
From there we went to the Carnegie Hall where we were supposed to play for Charlie Parker, but Charlie Parker got sick and was replaced by Sonny Stitt.
All right, we'll talk about that a little later when we get to '49. In that night, the first time you introduced Afro-Cuban jazz, January 24, 1947, at Town Hall, how long were you on stage?
